skeleton:
Full English Breakfast Pie

British · Medium · Serves 4

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English baked into a pie: a buttery shortcrust case loaded with a bacon, sausage, and black pudding filling bound in a savory egg custard, baked until the filling sets and the pastry turns deep gold. Somewhere between a quiche and a pork pie in spirit, it is the dish that turns breakfast into a picnic, a brunch into a centrepiece, and last night's fry-up philosophy into a cold slab you can eat with your hands at a football match. The technique is custard-pie discipline: the case is blind-baked to withstand a wet filling, the components are pre-cooked and cooled (raw sausage in a custard releases its water and floods the set), and the custard itself is built on the double-cream-and-egg ratio that sets to a tender slice rather than a rubbery one.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The pastry

The filling

The custard

- **Blind-bake the case:** the custard is wet and an unbaked base goes soggy in minutes. 20 minutes at 200 °C with baking paper and baking beans, then 5 minutes more naked, until the base is sandy-dry and just golden. This single step is the pie's structural insurance. - **Cook and cool every filling component.** Crumbled sausage browned through, bacon cooked to just-done (it bakes further), mushrooms browned dry, black pudding lightly seared — all cooled 10 minutes before the custard meets them. Hot components scramble the custard on contact and weep water into the set. - **The custard's ratio is the pie's texture:** 4 eggs to 200 ml cream plus 100 ml milk sets to a sliceable-but-tender custard. More milk and it weeps; more egg and it rubberises.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Shell: blind-baked to sandy-dry, holds a wet filling without soaking.
  • Filling components: all cooked, cooled, and dry before the custard.
  • Custard: 4:200:100 ratio, whisked homogenous, poured to 5 mm below the rim.
  • Bake: pulled at the centre wobble; rested 20 minutes; slices as a clean wedge.

Full English Breakfast Pie

Prep: 30 minutes · Cook: 50 minutes · Total: About 1 hour 20 minutes · Serves 4

Ingredients

The pastry

  • 200 g plain flour
  • 100 g cold butter, cubed
  • 1 large egg (55 g), beaten
  • 2 g fine sea salt
  • A splash of ice water (about 15 ml), only if needed

The filling

  • 4 rashers (200 g) back bacon, chopped
  • 3 pork sausages (240 g), skins removed, meat crumbled
  • 100 g black pudding, diced small
  • 100 g chestnut mushrooms, sliced and browned
  • 2 spring onions, sliced (30 g), or ½ small onion, sweated
  • 40 g mature Cheddar, grated

The custard

  • 4 large eggs (220 g)
  • 200 ml double cream
  • 100 ml whole milk
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 0.5 g ground nutmeg

Instructions

  1. **Make and rest the pastry.** Rub the butter into the flour and salt to breadcrumbs, mix in the egg to a dough — adding the ice water only if it refuses to come together — wrap, and chill 30 minutes. Roll to a 3 mm circle and line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tin, trimming the overhang. Chill again 15 minutes, then blind-bake as planned. Checkpoint — the blind-baked shell is evenly pale-gold with a dry, sandy base — no grey doughy patches, no bubbles. It should smell baked, not raw.
  2. **Cook the filling components.** In a frying pan over medium heat: brown the crumbled sausagemeat 6–7 minutes to cooked-through and crumbly; add the bacon for the last 4 minutes; the black pudding for the final 2; the mushrooms alongside until browned and dry. Tip everything to a bowl, cool 10 minutes, and fold in the spring onions and Cheddar. Checkpoint — every component cooked and cooling, the mushrooms dry (no weeping juice in the bowl's bottom), the mixture warm-not-hot.
  3. **Build the custard.** Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until completely homogenous — 30 seconds of vigorous whisking. Checkpoint — the custard is one even pale-yellow liquid with no streaks of white or yolk; a spoon dipped and lifted runs smooth.
  4. **Fill and bake — 35–40 minutes at 180 °C.** Scatter the filling evenly into the shell, pour the custard over (stop 5 mm short of the rim — it rises), and bake 35–40 minutes until the custard is set at the edges with a whisper of a wobble at the very centre, and the top is gold with freckles where the Cheddar caught. Checkpoint — the pie's centre wobbles as one when the tin is nudged — set, not sloshy, with the faintest tremor that carryover will finish. A knife inserted 3 cm from centre comes out clean-ish; wet batter means more time, and the foil shield goes on if the pastry's rim darkens early.
  5. **Rest 20 minutes, then slice.** The rest finishes the centre and sets the slice. Serve warm or at room temperature — the pie's party trick is that room temperature is its best temperature. Checkpoint — the cut slice holds as a clean wedge — pastry, custard, components in cross-section — and the eating is the full English in a new key: bacon and sausage and pudding suspended in a soft, savoury custard, the pastry's butter under everything.

Finish & Plate

Warm with brown sauce for the brunch table; cold with ketchup for the picnic; a wedge in the lunchbox with the mustard already spread on the pastry. The full English pie's true calling is the second day — overnight in the fridge firms the slice and marries the custard to the meats, which is why the recipe makes four servings for two people with a plan.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Soggy baseCase not blind-baked, or wet componentsThe full blind-bake; mushrooms and sausage cooked dry
Custard wept a ringOverbaked past the wobblePull earlier; the carryover is real
Filling floated in the custardComponents still hot when pouredThe 10-minute cool, always
Pastry rim burntOven fierce at the topA foil ring over the rim from minute 25

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **The keeper's dream:** 4 days refrigerated, slices firming and improving; freezes 2 months as whole or wedges. Assemble-and-bake-ahead: the blind-baked shell and cooked filling hold separately 2 days; assemble and bake on the morning. - **Variation — the beans-side pie:** serve with the smoky bacon baked beans warmed alongside — the plate's identity without the water risk inside the custard. - **Variation — the hash-brown crust:** the shell's base lined with 200 g of the wrung hash brown mix, pressed and blind-baked, the pastry as a top crust only — the potato-first restructure. - **The format trilogy:** pie (custard-set, sliceable), pizza (flat and fast), and pasty (handheld, sealed) — the full English's three baked forms, one philosophy: cook the components first, respect the water.
